summary: Connects to Ouster lidar sensors and outputs panoramic 32-bit floating point sensor data channels such as range, XYZ, signal, reflectivity, near IR, and flags.

key_params.name: deviceaddress
key_params.note: Sensor IP address or os-serial device name.

key_params.name: targetaddress
key_params.note: Target address the sensor sends data to.

key_params.name: scanmode
key_params.note: Choose scan resolution/rate mode such as mode512x10, mode1024x20, or mode4096x5.

key_params.name: opmode
key_params.note: Set sensor Normal or Standby operating mode.

key_params.name: dataformat
key_params.note: Set lidar packet format such as legacy, single, dual, or low data rate.

key_params.name: redchannel
key_params.note: Choose sensor data mapped to red.

key_params.name: greenchannel
key_params.note: Choose sensor data mapped to green.

key_params.name: bluechannel
key_params.note: Choose sensor data mapped to blue.

key_params.name: alphachannel
key_params.note: Choose sensor data mapped to alpha.

key_params.name: timemode
key_params.note: Internal OSC, Sync Pulse In, or PTP 1588 time sync.

common_gotchas: Official docs say Ouster TOP supports Windows and macOS ARM builds of TouchDesigner.
Only available in Educational, Commercial, and Pro licenses.
High-resolution scan modes can require up to 130 Mbps; Gigabit Ethernet is required for full operation.
Range values are in millimeters, while calculated XYZ positions are in meters.
TouchDesigner transforms 3D coordinates into its Y-up coordinate system, which differs from original Ouster coordinate space.
key_concepts: Connects to Ouster lidar sensors and receives high-bandwidth lidar packets.
Maps lidar channels such as range, signal, reflectivity, near IR, flags, and XYZ into RGBA data images.
GPU conversion can calculate 3D XYZ positions from beam azimuth and altitude tables.
Info CHOP access exposes IMU and timing data for sensor synchronization workflows.
Time sync can use internal OSC, sync pulse input, or PTP 1588 modes.
